title: Accounts Receivable Analyst
description:
It’s More Than a Career, It’s a Mission.
Our people are the foundation of our success. By joining our growing team at Sarah Cannon Research Institute (SCRI), a subsidiary of McKesson, you will have the opportunity to become part of one of the largest community-based cancer programs to advance oncology treatments and improve outcomes for cancer patients across the globe. We look for mission-driven candidates who have a desire to advance the fight against cancer and make a difference in the lives of patients diagnosed with cancer every day.
Our Mission
People who live with cancer - those who work to prevent it, fight it, and survive it - are at the heart of every decision we make. Bringing the most innovative medical minds together with the most passionate caregivers in their communities, we are transforming care and personalizing treatment. Through clinical excellence and cutting-edge research, SCRI is redefining cancer care around the world.

Job Description
Our Accounts Receivable Specialist is responsible for the reconciliation of client receivables in accordance with contractual agreements. Includes review of all Clinical Trial revenues and expenses, as well as interaction with various departments in order to determine the validity of charges and payments received from sponsors.

This is a remote position based in the US; relocation assistance and visa sponsorship are not available.

Duties include and are not limited to :

• Reconcile in detail clinical trial receivables to ensure final billing to pharmaceutical companies is accurate and timely

• Reconcile Sarah Cannon financial study data across multiple sources.

• Review and interpret contracts and budgets

• Work with operations and other departments to resolve variances

• Respond to requests for information from Corporate, Internal Audit, Operations and Management

• Perform Analysis of contracted revenue triggers to determine eligibility for reimbursement.

• Ensure that all processing and reporting deadlines are consistently achieved.

• Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications include:

• Bachelor's Degree required

• 1-2 years' work experience in Accounting or Finance in a medical, clinical trial research or healthcare-related environment

• Experience with Microsoft products including above average use of Excel and financial accounting systems such as Quickbooks.

• Knowledge of research techniques to analyze and evaluate financial data and information.

About Sarah Cannon Research Institute
Sarah Cannon Research Institute (SCRI) is one of the world’s leading oncology research organizations conducting community-based clinical trials. Focused on advancing therapies for patients over the last three decades, SCRI is a leader in drug development. In 2022, SCRI formed a joint venture with former US Oncology Research to expand clinical trial access across the country. It has conducted more than 850 first-in-human clinical trials since its inception and contributed to pivotal research that has led to the majority of new cancer therapies approved by the FDA in the past decade. SCRI’s research network brings together more than 1,300 physicians who are enrolling patients into clinical trials at more than 200 locations in 20+ states across the U.S. Please click here to learn more about our research offerings.

We care about the well-being of the patients and communities we serve, and that starts with caring for our people. That’s why we have a Total Rewards package that includes comprehensive benefits to support physical, mental, and financial well-being. Our Total Rewards offerings serve the different needs of our diverse colleague population and ensure they are the healthiest versions of themselves. For more information regarding benefits through our parent company, McKesson, please click here.

As a Financial Crimes Compliance Specialist, you will play a key role in supporting the Financial Crimes Compliance program for DraftKings Predictions, helping strengthen regulatory oversight, risk management, and monitoring initiatives within an evolving prediction markets environment. In this role, you'll collaborate cross-functionally with Compliance, Risk, Product, and Analytics teams to identify emerging financial crimes risks, enhance compliance controls, and ensure alignment with internal AML policies and applicable regulatory requirements. You'll also support governance, quality assurance, and program improvement initiatives that help protect our customers and support the continued growth of DraftKings Predictions.
What you’ll do as a Financial Crimes Compliance Specialist, Predictions

• Serve as a Financial Crimes Compliance subject matter expert, providing guidance and support to Compliance, Risk, and key business partners supporting DraftKings Predictions.

• Analyze regulatory requirements, industry trends, emerging financial crimes risks, and program effectiveness within prediction markets and trading environments.

• Advise on development of product features and functionality to manage risk and ensure compliance as effectively possible.

• Collaborate with internal teams to design and optimize transaction monitoring alerts and controls to improve the detection of potentially suspicious activity.

• Support internal risk assessments and assist with external audits and regulatory responses to ensure compliance with applicable laws, standards, and internal policies.

• Act as the point of contact for compliance-related escalations from team members, business partners, stakeholders, and third parties.

• Stay current with evolving AML regulations, financial crimes typologies, trading-related risks, and industry best practices to support ongoing program improvements.

What you’ll bring

• A Bachelor's Degree in a related field with at least 4 years of relevant AML, or other financial crimes related experience.

• Compliance or Risk Management certifications such as CAMS, CIPP, or CRCM, or willingness to obtain recommended certifications is preferred.

• Experience supporting compliance oversight, risk assessments, market surveillance, transaction monitoring, or quality assurance initiatives.

• Prior experience in trading, financial markets, prediction markets, brokerage, or other regulated financial services environments.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to assess complex information, identify potential risks, and recommend practical improvements.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex compliance requirements and collaborate effectively across teams.

• Highly organized with strong attention to detail, with the ability to manage competing priorities and adapt to evolving regulatory requirements and business needs.

• Project & Program Managers

•
Solution Architects (Commerce, CRM, CPQ, ServiceNow, Salesforce)

•
Work in the Gray, Deliver in Full Color: We perform where others pause. In complex, ambiguous environments, we lean in, ask smarter questions, see hidden angles, and solution a path forward-delivering value where it's hardest to find.

•
Act with Speed and Urgency: Speed is strategy. We move with discipline and urgency because timing changes everything. Our pace creates momentum, opportunity, and keeps us a step ahead, together.

Challenge Convention: We think differently so we can deliver differently. We question assumptions, reframe challenges, and step outside comfort zones to find smarter, sharper solutions. When others stick to what’s known, we push toward what’s next.

•
Own It. All Of It: We give a damn. Accountability is our operating system; we sweat the details and own the outcomes. If something’s not right, we fix it. If there’s a better way, we find it. No excuses. Just results and growth.

•
Stand Out By Design: We design every experience with intent-from how we engage clients to how we deliver solutions and shape culture. Nothing is accidental. Every detail is crafted to create clarity, impact, and connection-we use design as a mindset-for how we work, how we partner, and how we show up.

Who Should Apply

• Have experience in consulting, enterprise technology, manufacturing, or B2B environments

• Enjoy solving complex problems and working directly with clients

• Are comfortable with ambiguity and excited by growth

• Take pride in your work and care deeply about doing the right thing

• Want to help build-not just join-a company

• Grow alongside a team of experienced, collaborative leaders

• Have real ownership and influence as the company scales

• Be part of a culture that values people, purpose, and progress

If you don’t see a specific role that matches your background today-but believe you align with our values and mission-we encourage you to apply. We review general applications regularly and will reach out as opportunities arise.

Own your opportunity to deliver high‑quality, secure, and compliant technology in support of critical healthcare initiatives. As an Automation Tester at GDIT, you’ll power innovation through robust automated testing frameworks, advanced validation methods, and seamless coordination across engineering teams working in a modern Azure‑native environment.
MEANINGFUL WORK AND PERSONAL IMPACT
As an Automation Tester, the work you’ll do at GDIT will support the development, security, and reliability of a new healthcare portal operating in a FedRAMP/HIPAA‑compliant environment. You will play a crucial role in ensuring applications, APIs, microservices, and data flows perform flawlessly and securely, contributing directly to mission‑critical healthcare service delivery.

• Develop, execute, and maintain automated and manual test plans, test cases, and test scripts for web applications, APIs, microservices, and data workflows.
● Design and maintain automated testing solutions using Playwright (JavaScript) and Selenium (Java).
● Conduct functional, integration, regression, smoke, performance, accessibility, and user acceptance testing.
● Collaborate closely with front‑end, back‑end, data engineering, and DevOps teams to ensure smooth and reliable integration testing across multiple services.
● Perform API testing to validate payloads, authentication flows, error handling, and end‑to‑end behavior.
● Use SQL Server and SSMS to perform advanced database validation across large‑scale datasets using complex queries, multi‑table joins, CTEs, aggregations, and data comparisons.
● Validate data integrity across Azure SQL, Data Factory pipelines, and Power BI outputs.
● Ensure compliance with Section 508 accessibility standards and execute accessibility testing.
● Document defects, track issues in JIRA, maintain test artifacts in Confluence and SharePoint, and collaborate with developers to drive timely resolution.
● Support CI/CD pipelines through test automation integration and reporting within Azure DevOps.
● Participate in Agile ceremonies to ensure test readiness throughout development cycles.
● Contribute to continuous improvement of QA processes, tooling, frameworks, and quality practices.
● Work independently on complex features and integrations while maintaining strong collaboration with cross‑functional teams.

WHAT YOU’LL NEED TO SUCCEED
Bring your automation expertise and precision to GDIT. The Automation Tester must have:

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or related field, or equivalent experience
● 3-5+ years of experience in QA testing for web applications and APIs
● Hands-on experience with Playwright (JavaScript) or Selenium automation
● Strong SQL experience using SQL Server/SSMS, including advanced queries, CTEs, multi-table joins, and relational analysis
● Experience testing in Azure environments, including API, function, and database validation
● Proven experience with API testing tools and methods for validating workflows and responses
● Integration testing experience with the ability to coordinate across multiple teams
● Knowledge of Section 508 compliance and accessibility testing
● Experience with Agile tools and practices using JIRA, Confluence, and SharePoint

We’re building a world of health around every individual - shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger - helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.
Do you have a passion for engaging with people and helping them on their journey to better health? Signify Health, part of CVS Health®, is seeking a Part Time Clinician (Nurse Practitioner or Physician Assistant) to provide In-Home Health Evaluations, engaging with people in the comfort of their own homes and helping bridge gaps in care.
You’ll play a critical role in building trusted relationships to make people healthier, helping bring flexible, comprehensive and personalized health evaluations right to people’s front doors.
Job highlights
The visit, which lasts about 45 minutes, allows for time to connect one-on-one and answer health questions. It includes a medication and medical history review, a physical evaluation, and, if ordered by the person’s health plan, additional diagnostic tests (i.e., diabetic eye exams, spirometry, etc.). You’ll use an iPad and an intuitive clinical workflow for each evaluation and are not required to prescribe medicine, order lab tests or alter people’s current treatment regimen.
In this role, you will:

• Bring your heart into every visit, joining a national network of purpose-driven clinicians dedicated to improving health outcomes

• Be part of our efforts to visit millions of people nationwide with the goal of providing connections to the right care for people’s unique needs

• Work with Signify Health as a clinician colleague, fulfilling the requirements of the specified role

• Be flexible to travel locally and within licensed states, as needed

• Conduct virtual visits as needed

• Provide all Signify Health services as indicated including Diagnostic & Preventive Services products (i.e., spirometry, DEE, bone density screening, etc.)

A Note on Our Work Environment:
As an in-home clinician, your primary workplace is the private residence of health plan members. We are dedicated to meeting health plan members where they are, wherever they call home. These environments are diverse and may present a variety of conditions. Candidates must be able to comfortably and safely perform their duties in homes that may contain household pets, secondhand smoke and other potential airborne allergens or irritants.
Why Clinicians Enjoy Working with Signify Health
“I love seeing health plan members at home. You get a better picture of their health when you see where they live.” - Erica R., PA
“At Signify Health, we have the time to help people and to truly listen to their questions and concerns. We can help guide them so they can take better care of themselves. We really can make a change in communities.” - Ali B., NP

At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. The visit, which lasts about 45 minutes, allows for time to connect one-on-one and answer health questions. It includes a medication and medical history review, a physical evaluation, and, if ordered by the person’s health plan, additional diagnostic tests (i.e., diabetic eye exams, spirometry, etc.). In this role, you will:

• Bring your heart into every visit, joining a national network of purpose-driven clinicians dedicated to improving health outcomes

• Be part of our efforts to visit millions of people nationwide with the goal of providing connections to the right care for people’s unique needs

• Work with Signify Health as a clinician colleague, fulfilling the requirements of the specified role

• Be flexible to travel locally and within licensed states, as needed

• Conduct virtual visits as needed

• Provide all Signify Health services as indicated including Diagnostic & Preventive Services products (i.e., spirometry, DEE, bone density screening, etc.)

A Note on Our Work Environment:
As an in-home clinician, your primary workplace is the private residence of health plan members. We are dedicated to meeting health plan members where they are, wherever they call home. These environments are diverse and may present a variety of conditions. Candidates must be able to comfortably and safely perform their duties in homes that may contain household pets, secondhand smoke and other potential airborne allergens or irritants.
Why Clinicians Enjoy Working with Signify Health
“Many of the people I see are shocked that a physician is coming to their home to visit with them one-on-one. When you sit down and have an unhurried conversation about their health, they are impressed, happy, and understand that their health plan and care team cares about them.” - M.L., MD

We can make referrals to the individual’s health plan, encourage the participation of their loved ones, and ensure their PCPs are aware of their health and overall quality of life.” - C.H., MD

title: Email Infrastructure & Deliverability Specialist
description:
Floowi connects top LATAM professionals with leading U.S. companies through remote talent solutions. Our mission is to make LATAM the world’s premier hub for growth and excellence.
🌟 About our Client:
Our client specializes in performance-based customer database monetization, helping businesses generate recurring revenue from existing customer lists through consent-based marketing campaigns. Its multichannel approach includes email, SMS, and paid media, with campaigns funded by the company and revenue shared with its partners.
✍ Short Description:
We are looking for an Email Infrastructure & Deliverability Specialist to build, launch, and manage a high-volume email-sending infrastructure from the ground up. This role will own the technical setup and ongoing operation of the email-sending environment, including the selection and configuration of appropriate sending platforms and infrastructure. The specialist will manage campaigns across new and legacy contact lists, with a focus on inbox placement, sender reputation, and reliable delivery at scale. The goal is to establish a sustainable email operation capable of supporting approximately 300,000-500,000 emails per day while maintaining strong deliverability and responsible list management.
🌎 Location: 100% Remote (LATAM only)
🗣 Language Requirements: Advanced English (C1+)
⏰ Schedule: Full-time, aligned with EST
😀 Start Date: ASAP
💰 Compensation & Benefits:

• Competitive salary in USD, starting at $3,750/month

• Remote-first flexibility. Work from anywhere.

• PTO and paid U.S. holidays

💼 Responsibilities:

• Build and implement the email-sending infrastructure from scratch, selecting and configuring the platforms and technical components required for high-volume email delivery.

• Configure and maintain email authentication and sending infrastructure to support reliable delivery and protect sender reputation.

• Develop and manage a scalable sending operation capable of supporting approximately 300,000-500,000 emails per day.

• Plan, execute, and monitor bulk email campaigns across new and legacy contact lists, managing sending volumes and delivery performance.

• Monitor inbox placement, sender reputation, bounces, complaints, and other deliverability metrics to identify issues and implement corrective actions.

• Maintain and optimize the infrastructure and sending processes on an ongoing basis, adapting operations to campaign performance and evolving delivery requirements.

• Review, segment, and manage contact lists based on data quality, consent status, and engagement considerations to support sustainable campaign performance.

💡 Qualifications:

• Demonstrated experience building email-sending infrastructure from scratch and managing it on an ongoing basis.

• Proven experience operating high-volume email campaigns, ideally at a scale comparable to hundreds of thousands of emails per day.

• Strong technical knowledge of email deliverability, inbox placement, sender reputation, and email authentication protocols, including SPF, DKIM, and DMARC.

• Hands-on experience configuring and managing bulk email-sending platforms and the infrastructure required to operate them at scale.

• Experience monitoring delivery metrics, troubleshooting deliverability issues, and optimizing sending practices based on performance data.

• Experience managing new and legacy contact lists, including list quality, segmentation, consent considerations, bounces, and unsubscribe management.

📩 If you meet the experience outlined above, we’d love to hear from you. Please apply, our team is excited about your application and will be in touch as soon as possible.

title: Director, Clinical Operations
description:
About Lifeforce

We are in the early stages of a generational shift in how people approach their health. No longer satisfied with the reactive, fragmented care offered by the traditional healthcare system, millions of people are taking a more proactive approach. They want to understand how their bodies work, take control of how they feel and perform, and invest in living longer, healthier lives. Lifeforce is leading this shift as the world's largest longevity medicine program.

Founded alongside clinical and scientific leaders from Cleveland Clinic, Massachusetts General Hospital, and Harvard Medical School, Lifeforce brings together the diagnostics, expertise, and treatments people need to understand and optimize their health, both today and for decades to come. Our comprehensive program combines advanced diagnostics, expert clinicians, dedicated health coaches, and personalized supplement, pharmaceutical, and lifestyle protocols. All delivered from home, at the price of a gym membership.

Overview

Lifeforce is hiring a Director, Clinical Operations to run the operating engine behind our national proactive care delivery model. You'll own how clinicians get licensed, credentialed, onboarded, scheduled, supported, and reviewed for quality, and you'll make sure all of it holds up as we grow.

And we're growing fast. Our network of 50+ physicians, nurse practitioners, and physician assistants is expected to more than triple over the next 15 months, across a growing number of states. At the same time, we're opening physical longevity centers and the clinicians supporting those centers run through this role too. The systems that work for a network of 50 won't work at 200, and this role is the one that gets us there ahead of demand rather than behind it.

This is primarily an operations leadership role, not a clinical one. Clinical standards and clinical judgment stay with the Medical Director and clinical leadership. You'll own the people, processes, systems, and data that let clinicians do their best work at scale. You'll report to the COO and lead four teams: Clinical Operations, Clinical Onboarding & Enablement, Credentialing & Licensing, and Clinical Quality Assurance. You'll start with a small team and build it out to about 15 people by the end of 2027.

Key Responsibilities

Capacity & Scheduling

• Own clinician capacity planning against member demand, state by state. Know where we'll be short a quarter before it happens.

• Own clinician scheduling, including how appointments are assigned across telehealth, nurse services, and our centers, and how continuity of care is protected as the network grows. Work with Product and Engineering to build the tools for scheduling that the teams need.

• Track utilization, panel concentration, and access (time to next appointment), and act when they drift.

Hire to Productive

• Own the full clinician pipeline after the offer: licensure, credentialing, onboarding, training, and ramp to full schedule.

• Set and hit targets for time to credentialed and time- to-productive, and fix the bottlenecks in between.

• Build a licensure and DEA strategy that ensures compliance and keeps pace with growth.

Quality & Clinician Performance

• Own the operations of the clinical QA program, so every clinician is reviewed on schedule and the results reach the people who need them. The Clinical QA Lead reports to you, with a dotted line to the Medical Director on clinical standards.

• Build the operating process for clinician performance management with the Medical Director and clinical leadership. They own the clinical judgment; you own the cadence, data, documentation, and follow-through.

• Make sure the review approach and the follow-up fit our independent contractor model.

SOPs, Systems & Change Management

• Own the clinical SOP lifecycle: intake, drafting with clinical owners, approval, rollout, and retirement, with Guru as the system of record.

• Run changes so clinicians hear about them onc

title: Growth Manager (m/f/d)
description:
Wir verwalten über 70.000 Einheiten in ganz Deutschland. Das ist nicht das Geschäft, das ist die Plattform. Darauf bauen wir neue Verticals auf: Versicherung, Energie, Finanzierung und Brokerage. Für Brokerage suchen wir jetzt die Person, die daraus ein echtes Geschäft macht.

Darum geht es

Viele unserer Eigentümer wollen irgendwann verkaufen oder neu vermieten. Wir sitzen direkt an der Quelle und kennen Objekte, Eigentümer und Timing. Deine Aufgabe ist, daraus eine planbare Akquise-Maschine zu bauen: Du identifizierst die richtigen Eigentümer aus unserem Bestand, sprichst sie gezielt an und wandelst erstes Interesse in hochqualifizierte Leads für unsere Makler um.

Das ist keine Strategie-Rolle mit Folien und Roadmaps. Du baust selbst: Kampagnen, Outbound-Workflows, Automatisierungen, Funnels. Du weißt jede Woche, welche Zahl du bewegt hast. Du arbeitest direkt mit dem Leadership-Team, ohne Hierarchie-Ebenen dazwischen.

Was du machst

- Akquise-Engine aufbauen: Du analysierst unseren Bestand, findest Eigentümer mit Verkaufs- oder Vermietungsbedarf und baust Workflows für Datenanreicherung, Lead-Scoring und automatisierte Ansprache.

- Marketing selbst umsetzen: Du baust und optimierst die Kanäle, die Leads bringen, von Outbound über Performance-Kampagnen bis zu In-App-Triggern im richtigen Moment.

- Funnel und Zahlen verantworten: Du definierst KPIs vom Lead bis zum Mandat, trackst Kosten pro Lead und Conversion und optimierst so lange, bis die Unit Economics stimmen.

- Schnell testen: Daten-Trigger, Kanäle, Messaging und Lead-Magneten. Du hast eine klare Meinung, was du ausprobieren willst, und misst es sauber.

Was du mitbringst

- 3+ Jahre operative Erfahrung in Growth oder Performance Marketing, mit eigener Verantwortung für Leads, Conversion oder Umsatz.

- Du hast Dinge von null aufgebaut, etwa als Gründer:in, als Geschäftsführer:in eines kleinen Unternehmens oder in einer frühen Startup-Phase. Das ist für uns ein starkes Signal.

- Hands-on-Erfahrung mit datengetriebener Akquise: Outbound, Datenanreicherung, CRM und Automatisierung.

- Marketing-Erfahrung mit Performance-Kanälen und Kampagnen ist ein klares Plus.

- Erfahrung in Immobilien, PropTech oder Marktplätzen ist ein Plus, aber kein Muss.

- Verhandlungssicheres Deutsch (mindestens C1). Du sprichst täglich mit Eigentümern und unseren Hausverwaltungen.

- Du lebst in Berlin oder ziehst her und reist gern zu unseren Standorten in ganz Deutschland.

Bitte nicht bewerben, wenn

- du vor allem Strategie machen und die Umsetzung anderen überlassen willst,

- du erst ein Team führen möchtest, bevor das Modell bewiesen ist,

- du nicht bereit bist, in Berlin zu arbeiten.

Was wir bieten

- Ein Vertical, das du von Anfang an prägst, mit 70.000 Einheiten als Basis und voller Rückendeckung vom Leadership-Team.

- Ein Inside-Sales-Team, auf das du zugreifen kannst: Es übernimmt Anrufe und die Bearbeitung deiner Kampagnen, damit du dich auf den Aufbau der Akquise-Engine konzentrieren kannst.

- Einen direkten Weg zur Verantwortung: Wenn Brokerage funktioniert, skalierst du es weiter.

- Top-Vergütung inklusive virtueller Aktienoptionen und 500 € Wohnzuschuss pro Monat in der Nähe unseres Büros.

- 110 € Lunch-Budget und 50 € Fitness-Zuschuss pro Monat, täglich Frühstück und Spezialitäten-Kaffee im Office.

- 1.200 € Weiterbildungsbudget pro Jahr.

We recently post-trained our first model built for legal work, and we’re now building the team to scale up our post-training efforts. Learn more about our work at harvey.ai/research http://harvey.ai/research.

- Own and pursue a research agenda to improve model capability on long-horizon legal reasoning and agentic workflows.

- Design and run post-training experiments across SFT and RL, building on leading open-weight models.

- Develop reward functions and verifiers for semi-verifiable tasks, including rubrics, learned preference models, and expert preference data, and study where they break.

- Run and debug training at scale, addressing divergence, reward hacking, and instability.

- Build and use rigorous evals to track improvements and decide what ships.

- Design, implement, test, and debug code across our research stack.

WHAT YOU HAVE

- Hands-on experience post-training LLMs with SFT and RL, including preference optimization, and direct ownership of training runs and results.

- Deep ML fundamentals and experience getting distributed training runs working reliably.

- Strong engineering skills in Python, with production-quality code and end-to-end system ownership.

- Research experience in RL for language models or reward modeling, with the ability to move quickly from experiments to shipped improvements. Publications welcome, not required.

We are hiring for this role across multiple levels.

$230,000 - $340,000 USD

Finance teams at B2B companies lose cash the same way every month: an invoice ages past 45 days, someone sends an email, no reply, someone calls, voicemail, they call again next week, still nothing. Argentl delivers an AI collections agent that handles outbound debtor follow-up automatically - trained, monitored, and continuously improved by our team. WHAT YOU’LL BRING

title: Local Reporting Network Fellow
description:
ProPublica is an independent, nonprofit newsroom that produces investigative journalism in the public interest.

ProPublica ’s Local Reporting Network helps produce vital, investigative journalism in communities where such stories would otherwise not be done. Now entering its ninth year, the program will be taking on 15 new partnerships over the course of 2026.
Applications for all 15 projects are open now and will be considered on a rolling basis using the deadlines below. There will be three fellowship periods and we will select five fellows for each round:

• Spring cohort - This round is now closed.

•
Application deadline: Rolling, no later than Feb. 5, 2026, by 11:59 p.m. ET.

•
Open to: All applicants from English-language local and regional newsrooms in the United States and its territories.

•
Fellowship dates: April 1, 2026, through March 31, 2027.

• Summer cohort. This round is now closed

•
Application deadline: Rolling, no later than May 1, 2026.

•
Open to: Newsrooms in the states listed as eligible through our 50 State Initiative.

•
Fellowships dates: July 1, 2026, through June 30, 2027.

• Fall cohort

•
Application deadline: Rolling, no later thanJuly 27, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. ET.

•
Open to: Newsrooms in the remaining states listed as eligible through our 50 State Initiative. (Note: This list of states will be updated in July 2025.)

•
Fellowship dates: Oct. 1, 2026, through Sept. 30, 2027.

For these partnerships, ProPublica will provide a grant, to be paid in monthly installments, to the selected newsroom reflecting the annual salary (up to $80,000 plus a 25% allowance for benefits) for one full-time reporter in each newsroom. Successful candidates will have a proven track record of investigative reporting and impact, and will provide a memo about the project they’re proposing working on for the duration of the one-year partnership.
Strong applications will express why the project needs to be told in your community - we’re eager for projects that can’t be done anywhere else. They will also explain how the project would benefit from this collaboration, potentially including the role that our data, research and engagement reporting resources could play, and they will discuss how the project may resonate with both local and national audiences.
Once accepted, local reporters will work from and report to their home newsrooms while receiving extensive support and guidance for their work from ProPublica , including collaboration with a senior editor and access to the nonprofit newsroom’s expertise. The work will be published or broadcast by your newsroom and simultaneously by ProPublica .
ProPublica reporters and editors are available to answer questions or to give you feedback on your application before you submit it. Please reach us at .
We are unable to accept applications via email. No phone calls, please.

We know there are great candidates who may not fit into what we’ve described above or who have important skills we haven’t thought of. If that’s you, don’t hesitate to apply and tell us about yourself.

We are dedicated to improving our newsroom, in part by better reflecting the people we cover. (Here is a breakdown of our staff.) We are committed to diversity and building an inclusive environment for people of all backgrounds and ages. And we are taking steps to meet that commitment. We especially encourage members of traditionally underrepresented communities to apply, including women, people of color, LGBTQ+ people and people with disabilities. We are an equal opportunity employer and prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind. All employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, age or any other status protected under applicable law.

Job Title: Scrum Master
Term: 12 months
Location: Nairobi, Kenya

Level: Intermediate/ Senior (4-8 years of relevant experience).
Key Responsibilities

• Own and maintain the team's delivery metrics dashboard (sprint velocity, burndown/burnup, defect rates, cycle time, cumulative flow), surfacing trends and escalating concerns to the TPM.

• Actively identify, track, and remove constraints blocking squad members from delivering sprint goals; escalate cross-organizational blockers to the TPM within agreed SLAs.

• Coach squad members and relevant stakeholders on agile principles, Scrum practices, and delivery best practices, progressively building internal agile capability.

• Facilitate cross-squad coordination where multiple technical work streams (Backend, Frontend, API, Data) have interdependent sprint commitments.

• Support knowledge transfer by ensuring that process documentation, decision logs, and sprint artefacts are maintained in the agreed shared workspace.

• Report on delivery health metrics at fortnightly steering cadence, partnering with the TPM for programme-level reporting.

Measurable Outcomes & Deliverables
First 30 Days

• Attend all Scrum ceremonies and produce baseline assessment of ceremony health, compliance, and documentation gaps.

• Own the delivery metrics dashboard and report on velocity, burndown, defect rates, and cycle time and report any present gaps.

• Produce a cross-squad dependency register across Backend, Frontend, API, and Data workstreams.

• Confirm fortnightly steering cadence with the TPM and key stakeholders.

Days 31-60

• Sprint velocity stabilizing; at least two consecutive sprints with 80% sprint goal achievement.

• DoD compliance rate tracked and reported; 90% of completed stories meet DoD criteria.

• Backlog health confirmed: two sprints of stories refined and sprint-ready at all times.

• At least one agile coaching session delivered to client counterparts or junior squad members.

• Delivery metrics dashboard live and shared with TPM and stakeholders.

Days 61-90

• Retrospective improvement actions tracked; demonstrable improvement in at least two delivery metrics since sprint 1.

• Agile maturity assessment (informal) of squad completed; coaching plan for remaining engagement period produced.

• All sprint ceremonies running to time and rated as useful by squad members (informal pulse check).

• Knowledge transfer - one squad member or stakeholder who has visibly adopted improved Scrum practices through coaching

Ongoing KPIs

• Enable the squad to consistently achieve agreed sprint goals through effective planning and execution.

• Ensure stories meet the agreed Definition of Done before acceptance.

• Proactively identify, escalate, and facilitate resolution of delivery blockers and dependencies.

• Maintain a healthy, prioritized backlog that supports upcoming sprint planning and delivery.

• Drive continuous improvement by facilitating effective sprint ceremonies and retrospectives and ensuring agreed improvement actions are followed through.

Stakeholders & Ways of Working
Agile Ceremonies Owned: Sprint planning, daily stand-ups, sprint reviews, retrospectives, backlog refinement.
Reporting Cadence:

• Fortnightly delivery health summary to TPM.

• Sprint metrics dashboard updated at end of each sprint.

• Ad-hoc impediment escalation to TPM as required.

Cross-Functional Touchpoints:

• All squad roles (API Engineer, Backend, Frontend, Data Scientist, UI/UX Designer).

• Product Owners and stakeholders attending sprint reviews.

• TPM for programme-level dependency and risk alignment.

Required Skills & Experience

It extends privileged access management from the point of access to the moment of action, using just-in-time authorization to reduce standing privilege across on-premises, multi-cloud and short-lived infrastructure, without adding friction for legitimate users. Delinea provides visibility across every identity type, scores the risk each one carries, and preserves the context behind access decisions, making them auditable and defensible. It supports both static and ephemeral access, letting teams apply Zero Standing Privilege where risk demands it without replacing existing infrastructure.

Summary:

Delinea’s Cybersecurity organization is seeking an experienced and highly skilled Technical Program Manager to contribute to the planning, execution, and delivery of Delinea’s Enterprise Security program and initiatives.

This role will be responsible for evolving the Enterprise Security program, driving execution across multiple initiatives, and play a critical part in ensuring the timely and effective implementation of enterprise security initiatives and aligning efforts with organizational goals.

The ideal candidate will possess a strong technical background in security operations, security engineering, and program management, with a proven ability to collaborate with engineering, IT, product, and security leaders and manage complex, large-scale initiatives.

This is a remote role that is based in the United States and reports to the Sr. Director of Enterprise Security.

What You'll Do:

- Manage the Enterprise Security program portfolio, including intake, prioritization, planning, scheduling, and resource allocation across IAM, Security Operations, and Security Engineering.

- Drive end-to-end delivery of cross-functional security initiatives, such as identity lifecycle and access governance, privileged access, authentication and MFA improvements, SIEM and EDR deployments or migrations, managed security service onboarding, and security tooling rollouts.

- Build and maintain integrated roadmaps and project plans with team leads, defining scope, milestones, dependencies, and success criteria for each initiative.

- Identify, track, and manage risks, issues, dependencies, and decisions, escalating blockers early and driving them to resolution.

- Define and maintain program metrics and key performance indicators (KPIs) and produce regular status reports and executive-ready updates for security leadership.

- Coordinate audit and compliance-driven work, including control remediation, evidence collection, and tracking findings to closure in support of commitments such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, and FedRAMP.

- Partner with stakeholders to align priorities, secure resources, and manage organizational change for security initiatives that affect employees and business processes.

- Support vendor and contract management for security tools and services, including renewal timelines, deployment milestones, and budget tracking.

- Coordinate tabletop exercises and post-incident follow-up, tracking lessons learned and corrective actions through completion.

- Establish and continuously improve program management processes, templates, and tooling for the Enterprise Security team.

- Collaborate with Technical Program Managers across Cybersecurity to capture inter-dependencies and ensure consistency in planning, tracking, and reporting.

- Maintain Enterprise Security program documentation, including roadmaps, program charters, runbooks, decision logs, and status updates.

What You'll Bring:

- Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Security, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

- 5+ years of experience in technical program or project management, with at least 2 years leading information security or IT infrastructure programs.

title: Media Relations Lead
description:
ABOUT FLUIDSTACK

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it.

We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.

We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

HOW WE OPERATE

- Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

- Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

- Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

- Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

- Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

THE PUBLIC AFFAIRS TEAM

Examples of key problems the team is working on

- Earn the public's permission to build at a pace no one has. Gigawatt campuses across all regions in the US, each needing community trust before steel goes up.

- Make Fluidstack the most welcomed builder in every town we enter. Local-first engagement, enforceable community commitments, and household bills that never carry our costs.

- Tell the story of American reindustrialization through the work itself. Third-party validators, local voices, and earned coverage that compounds as the portfolio grows.

ROLE SCOPE

- Own media relationships at the local, state, and national levels, giving backgrounds and coordinating on-the-record comments so Fluidstack's story is told accurately to the right audience at the right time.

- Partner with external PR firms across sites and states, briefing them and directing their work so company interests are represented and internal teams are fully supported.

- Run the local announcement playbook end to end for each new site: press releases, local media tours, open houses, and milestone moments from permits locked to ribbon cutting.

- Build briefing materials, Q&A, and prep for every spokesperson moment, from a county open house to a founder's national interview.

- Field and triage inbound press across a multi-state portfolio, knowing when to engage, when to background, and when silence is the strategic answer.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

- You've worked inside a PR agency and on the client side directing one, so you know how to brief a firm, push its work to the standard, and get full value from a retainer.

- You've run press in political or government settings where a single wrong quote carries real consequences, and your judgment on when not to engage is as sharp as your pitch.

- You've told the story of physical infrastructure at scale (data centers, energy, utilities, or large capital projects) to audiences ranging from skeptical locals to national reporters.

- You've created press events from scratch: announcements, open houses, site tours, ribbon cuttings, and the media moments that turn a milestone into coverage.

title: Senior GRC Engineer

Why join us

Brex is the intelligent finance platform that enables companies to spend smarter and move faster in more than 200 markets. By combining global corporate cards and banking with intuitive spend management, bill pay, and travel software, Brex enables founders and finance teams to accelerate operations, gain real-time visibility, and control spend effortlessly. Brex’s AI-native automation and world-class service eliminate manual expense and accounting tasks for customers so they can focus on what matters most. Working at Brex allows you to push your limits, challenge the status quo, and collaborate with some of the brightest minds in the industry. We make this a reality by empowering you with the tools, resources, and support you need to grow your career.

Our teams operate with high autonomy and deep collaboration, own outcomes end to end, and push for excellence from architecture to deployment. It’s an environment where engineering is a craft and builders grow by solving meaningful technical problems.

What you’ll do

As a Senior GRC Engineer at Brex, you’ll lead the IT security compliance workstreams that connect our technical control owners to the people who examine our controls: external auditors, Internal Audit, state regulators, and Finance. You’ll coordinate and test the technical controls behind our financial reporting (SOX/ITGC), our annual SOC 1 Type 2 report, our state money transmitter examinations, and our FINRA IT requirements. • Test quarterly user access reviews, privileged-access evidence, and segregation-of-duties remediation, and verify that in-scope changes are complete and properly authorized.

• Run the annual BC/DR testing calendar, including tabletop and failover exercises, and document results, evidence, and remediation.

• Prepare FINRA-related IT control documentation, including business continuity, books-and-records, systems access reviews, and readiness testing.

• Track findings through to closure with clear control owners, deadlines, and evidence, and keep audit coordination separate from control operation.

• Support broader GRC team operational tasks related to evidence collection, access requests, and risk management.

title: Senior Cloud Network Engineer
description:
ABOUT NU

Nu serves more than 140 million customers, guided by a mission to fight complexity and empower people. The company has been leading an industry transformation through innovative products and human-centered services.

 

Proprietary technology and data at scale power Nu’s digital platform, built to promote financial access, advancement, and transparency. Its business model thrives on customer love and lower costs, feeding a flywheel of growth and profitability.

Visit our Institutional Page https://www.nu.com/2026-en

ABOUT THE ROLE

Every transaction at Nubank travels across a network before it reaches a customer. As we grow across countries, accounts and regions, the connectivity layer underneath has to stay fast, segmented, auditable and cost-efficient, without ever becoming the thing that takes the platform down.

As a Senior Cloud Network Engineer on our Cloud Network platform engineering team, you will design, build and operate the cloud network that Nubank’s engineering teams rely on. You will treat the network as software: automated, tested and versioned. This is an IC5 role: you lead through technical depth, design quality and influence, not direct reports. You will be part of a global engineering organization and work with teammates across countries, so collaboration in English is part of everyday work.

You’ll be responsible for

- Designing and evolving connectivity patterns across multi-account, multi-region and hybrid-cloud topologies, making sound architectural decisions in designs that span multiple teams.

- Building and maintaining the network platform as code (Terraform or similar), with strong standards for testing, code review and reusable modules.

- Owning the operational health of the platform in your scope: leading incident response, driving postmortems and following through on the tech debt they uncover.

- Promoting safe change on the network: gradual rollouts, monitoring and fast rollback.

- Defining observability for the platform, with monitoring and SLAs that surface issues before customers feel them.

- Owning the network security posture of your scope, including segmentation and standards such as PCI DSS, with controls that hold up under audit.

- Simplifying the topology over time through consolidation, deprecation and paved roads, balancing scalability, maintainability and cost.

- Evaluating build vs. buy decisions with data on stability, scalability and cost.

- Mentoring other engineers, taking part in hiring, and documenting decisions so knowledge travels across teams.

We are looking for a person who has

- Production experience with public cloud networking, preferably AWS: Transit Gateway, VPC design, Direct Connect, PrivateLink, Route 53, NAT/egress patterns and network firewalls. Experience with Azure or GCP networking is also valued.

- Experience connecting cloud and on-premises environments: hybrid connectivity, BGP and dynamic routing, IP address management, load balancers and firewalls, planning, deploying and troubleshooting at scale.

- Coding and automation skills (Python, Go, Java, .NET), using infrastructure as code (Terraform or similar), Git, CI/CD and containers to build and operate network infrastructure.

- A background in network engineering, SRE, DevOps or software engineering. What matters is hands-on public cloud networking experience.

- Experience leading incident response and root cause analysis for high-impact failures that cross team boundaries.

CodeRabbit is the governance and control layer for agentic software development, helping engineering teams trust the code they ship. AI can generate code faster than people can review and understand it. Teams still need to know whether each change solves the right problem, fits their architecture, and is safe to ship.

We provide independent validation grounded in codebase context and team standards, giving people the evidence they need to judge what should ship. Across Review, Triage, Explain, and Secure, our platform challenges changes before merge, prioritizes pull requests by value, impact, and risk, explains what changed and why it matters, and monitors the codebase for security vulnerabilities after merge.

title: Agreements Manager
description:
The Agreements Manager is a strategic member of the Technology Development and Industry Engagement (TDIE) department responsible for advancing St. Jude Children's Research Hospital 's research, innovation, and technology commercialization objectives through the development, negotiation, and management of complex research and intellectual property agreements. This role plays a critical part in enabling scientific collaboration while safeguarding institutional interests, ensuring researchers have the contractual infrastructure necessary to pursue transformative discoveries that support the St. Jude mission of finding cures and saving children.

Serving as a trusted partner to investigators, institutional leaders, and external collaborators, the Agreements Manager oversees a diverse portfolio of agreements that facilitate research partnerships, technology transfer activities, intellectual property management, and industry engagement. The role provides strategic guidance throughout the agreement lifecycle, balancing scientific, operational, legal, and business considerations to support both near-term research objectives and long-term institutional goals.

As part of the TDIE team, the Agreements Manager helps bridge the gap between discovery and impact by enabling collaborations that accelerate the development and commercialization of innovative technologies, therapeutics, diagnostics, and research tools. Through effective negotiation, compliance oversight, relationship management, and stewardship of intellectual property assets, this position plays a vital role in maximizing the global reach and influence of St. Jude innovations while supporting the institution's commitment to advancing pediatric health worldwide.
